body.p: In the Office Action dated November 19, 2024, the Examiner rejects claims 4 and

8 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being indefinite, rejects claims 1-4, 6, 8, 14-16, and 20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103, and objects to claims 5, 7, 9-13, and 17-19 as allegedly being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the features of the base claim and any intervening claims. With this Supplemental Amendment, Applicant has amended claims 1, 2, 6, 7, 10, 11, 13, 14, and 20. Support for the amendments can be found throughout the specification, drawings, and claims as originally filed including, for example, at paragraphs [0055], [0056], [0060]-[0063], and [0083]-[0088]. After entry of this Amendment, claims 1-20 remain pending in the Application. Reconsideration of the Application as amended is respectfully requested.

Each of claims 5, 7, 9-13, and 17-19 is objected to as allegedly being dependent upon a rejected base claim, but would be allowable if rewritten in independent form including all of the features of the base claim and any intervening claims.
Applicant notes with appreciation the Examiner's consideration of these claims.
However, because each of claims 5, 7, 9-13, and 17-19 depends upon one of
independent claims 1 and 14, and because each of independent claims 1 and 14 is allowable at least for the reasons presented below, each of claims 5, 7, 9-13, and 17-19 is allowable.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw the objection to claims 5, 7, 9-13, and 17-19 and allow these claims.
Claims 4 and 8 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b) as allegedly being

indefinite. Applicant has amended each of independent claims 4 and 8 to address the issue identified by the Examiner. Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw the rejection of claims 4 and 8 under 35 U.S.C. § 112(b).

Claims 1-4, 6, 8, 14, and 20 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over a document by Raphael Stern et al. entitled "Dissipation of Stop-and-Go Waves Via Control of Autonomous Vehicles: Field Experiments" (Stern) in view of U.S. Publication No. 2018/0194352 to Avedisov et al. (Avedisov).

Claims 15 and 16 are rejected under 35 U.S.C. § 103 as allegedly being unpatentable over Stern in view of Avedisov and a document by Cathy Wu et al. entitled "Stabilizing Traffic via Autonomous Vehicles" (Wu).
Reconsideration is respectfully requested.
Features of claims 5, 7, and 9 have been incorporated into each of independent claims 1, 14, and 20.

None of Stern, Avedisov, or Wu is directed to changing "an ego vehicle speed to optimize a model of a cruise control system to correct the gap by adding a product of a gain multiplied by a difference to the model as a gap maintaining term, adding, in response to a condition in which an absolute value of a difference of the desired speed subtracted from the preceding vehicle speed being less than a threshold, at least one term to the model, or changing, in the model, a product of a gain multiplied by a first difference to account for a period of the stop-and-go cycle" as recited in each of independent claims 1, 14, and 20.
Accordingly, each of independent claims 1, 14, and 20 is patentable over Stern, Avedisov, and Wu.
Moreover, because each of claims 2-13 and 15-19 depends upon one of
independent claims 1 and 14, and because of the distinctive features recited in each of claims 2- 13 and 15-19, each of these claims is patentable over Stern, Avedisov, and Wu.
Therefore, Applicant respectfully requests that the Examiner reconsider and withdraw the rejection of claims 1-20 under 35 U.S.C. § 103.
Conclusion
It is submitted that this Amendment has antecedent basis in the Application as

originally filed, including the specification, claims and drawings, and that this Amendment does not add any new subject matter to the application. Reconsideration of the Application as amended is requested. It is respectfully submitted that this Amendment places the Application in suitable condition for allowance; notice of which is requested.
No fees are believed due in connection with this paper. Nonetheless, the
Commissioner is authorized to charge any fees which may be required in connection with this paper to Deposit Account Number 50-6747.

If the Examiner feels that prosecution of the present Application can be expedited by way of an Examiner's amendment, the Examiner is invited to contact the undersigned at the telephone number listed below.
